children: German 10-year Bund yields require a pronounced improvement in the Middle East, which could allow energy prices to decline, to return to SEB's target range below the current levels, chief rates strategist Jussi Hiljanen says in a note. "For the 10-year Bund to revert to our previous 3.10-3.30% target range, some positive news on the Iran conflict would likely be required," he says. Fading hopes of an Iran deal, the implications for European energy markets and the relatively resilient economy have contributed to higher bond yields across the curve, he says. The 10-year Bund yield closed at 3.35% on Thursday, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

title: German 10-Year Bund Yield Needs Good News from Middle East to Go Lower — Market Talk
